entries.title: Terminal partition cells and exterior sensitivity
entries.statement: A finite cell exposes distinct terminals T and a state pi, a partition of T recording connectivity inside the cell. On a common deterministic skeleton a crossing event is a Boolean function f of all cell partitions. Exterior sensitivity S_i(x_-i) equals one exactly when f(x_-i,pi) is nonconstant as pi ranges over the finite allowed cell states; it depends only on the exterior.
assumptions: Finite terminal sets and state spaces
Same deterministic skeleton and event in both compared laws

entries.title: DRAFT weighted independent-cell comparison
entries.statement: DRAFT author-proved partial result; independent referee review pending. For a Boolean event f on finitely many cell states, two product laws mu=product mu_i and nu=product nu_i satisfy |E_nu f-E_mu f|<=sum_i TV(mu_i,nu_i) P_Hi(S_i), where H_i has nu_j for j<i and mu_j for j>i, and S_i means the event is nonconstant in cell i for the fixed exterior. This does not prove the C0017 square-lattice scaling limit.
assumptions: Finite state sets with the same cell skeleton in both laws
Independence of all cell variables within each endpoint law
Boolean event f

entries.title: DRAFT finite independent-bond obstruction
entries.statement: DRAFT author-proved partial result; independent referee review pending. No finite undirected graph with three distinct terminal vertices and independent edges with probabilities strictly between zero and one induces a terminal partition law supported exactly on the all-separate and all-connected partitions with positive mass on both. For m fair edges in a graph connecting the three terminals, total variation from any such all-or-none law is at least 2^(-m). This does not prove the C0017 square-lattice scaling limit.
assumptions: Finite graph
Three distinct terminal vertices
Independent nondegenerate edge states
All-or-none target has all-connected mass p in (0,1)

entries.title: DRAFT pair matching crossing counterexample
entries.statement: DRAFT author-proved partial result; independent referee review pending. A three-edge independent star with edge probability 1/sqrt(2) matches all three pair-connection probabilities of a fair all-or-none site cell, yet the event that terminal a connects to b or c has probability 1-1/(2sqrt(2)), exceeding 1/2 by (1-1/sqrt(2))/2. This does not prove the C0017 square-lattice scaling limit.
assumptions: Three terminal star
Three mutually independent edges with common probability 1/sqrt(2)
Reference site cell joins all terminals with probability 1/2 and none otherwise

entries.title: DRAFT equal marginals crossing counterexample
entries.statement: DRAFT author-proved partial result; independent referee review pending. Equal one-cell marginals do not control a joint crossing event if cell independence is removed: X=(Z,Z) and Y=(Z,1-Z), Z fair, have identical marginals but P(X_1=X_2=1)=1/2 and P(Y_1=Y_2=1)=0. This does not prove the C0017 square-lattice scaling limit.
assumptions: Fair bit Z
The endpoint joint laws are the two stated dependent laws

entries.title: Refuted route: pair connectivity determines every crossing
entries.statement: REFUTED ROUTE, retained as a draft concept: matching all three pair-connectivity probabilities of a three-terminal cell was proposed to imply equality of every crossing event on a common skeleton. This implication is false: a star with three independent edges of probability 1/sqrt(2) matches each fair-site pair probability 1/2, but a connection from terminal a to the boundary set {b,c} has probability 1-1/(2sqrt(2)) rather than 1/2.
assumptions: Three distinct terminals
Full cell connectivity, rather than only one fixed pair event, can enter a crossing

entries.title: Refuted route: dependent cells substituted as products
entries.statement: REFUTED ROUTE, retained as a draft concept: applying the independent-cell comparison using only coordinate marginal total-variation distances for dependent endpoint laws is false. The laws of (Z,Z) and (Z,1-Z), for Z a fair bit, have identical coordinate marginals but probabilities 1/2 and 0 for the event that both bits equal one.
assumptions: Dependent joint laws are permitted in the refuted proposal

entries.title: Unresolved C0017 comparison gap G1
entries.statement: UNRESOLVED RESEARCH BRIDGE. For square-bond and triangular-site crossings in one marked Jordan domain, construct a common deterministic planar cell skeleton with independent partition laws mu_delta and nu_delta, representation errors r_mu(delta), r_nu(delta), and actual exterior hybrid laws H_i=(product_{j<i} nu_j)(product_{j>i} mu_j). Prove r_mu+r_nu+sum_i TV(mu_i,nu_i) P_Hi(S_i=1) tends to zero. The weighted comparison would then transfer the known reference crossing limit. No such construction or bound is proved in this packet. Neither the exponent 5/4 on square bonds nor uniform arm bounds for arbitrary hybrids may be assumed. Interface convergence still needs tightness and identification.
assumptions: Critical square-lattice independent bonds at p=1/2
Reference critical triangular-lattice independent sites at p=1/2
Uniform marked Jordan boundary approximation
No current-open or novelty claim

entries.title: DRAFT source correction: q=1 standard parafermionic spin
entries.statement: SOURCE CORRECTION DRAFT, pending independent review. For the standard FK edge observable F(e)=E[exp(i sigma W_gamma(e,e_b)) 1_{e in gamma}], with winding measured in radians and 0<sigma<1, the parameter convention sin(pi sigma/2)=sqrt(q)/2 gives sigma=1/3 at q=1; sigma=2/3 corresponds to q=3. The existing C0017 attempt card says q=1 has spin 2/3. This correction concerns that parameter only, not the conjectural observable limit or the remaining conformal-invariance gap. Primary reference: Duminil-Copin, Conjecture 1 Eq.(3.3), https://www.ihes.fr/~duminil/publi/divergenceFK.pdf .
assumptions: Standard stated edge-observable and winding convention
0<q<4, 0<sigma<1; specialize q=1
